note_claims.claim: The patient presented with a flare of rheumatoid arthritis lasting three weeks.
The patient experienced painful swelling of the right wrist and right hand knuckles for three weeks.
The patient has early morning stiffness lasting about 90 minutes (initially reported as 30 minutes).
The patient has mild foot ache.
The patient experiences mild nausea the day after taking methotrexate.
The patient drinks about six units of alcohol per week.
The patient's husband had shingles last month.
The patient had chickenpox as a child.
The patient has not had shingles.
The patient is currently taking methotrexate 15 mg once weekly on Mondays.
The patient is taking folic acid 5 mg once weekly on Thursdays.
The patient has a history of a rash associated with sulfasalazine.
The examination revealed synovitis of the right wrist and the right second and third MCP joints.
The left hand examination was normal.
The patient's CRP is 28.
The patient's blood count and liver tests are normal.
The disease activity score is 4.8, indicating moderate activity.
The clinical impression is a rheumatoid arthritis flare with moderate disease activity on methotrexate.
The plan is to increase methotrexate to 20 mg once weekly on Mondays.
The plan is to continue folic acid 5 mg once weekly on Thursdays.
The plan is to administer a steroid injection (methylprednisolone 120 mg) today to settle the flare.
The plan is to repeat blood tests every two weeks for the next six weeks, then every three months.
The patient is scheduled for a clinic review in three months.

Safety netting advises stopping methotrexate and getting an urgent blood test if the patient develops a sore throat, fever, mouth ulcers, unusual bruising or bleeding, or a new cough or breathlessness.
Safety netting advises reporting a painful blistering rash promptly.
